thread:
Talia Mendes: Spotted during today's design pass: when rotating the device (mobile) the console header reflows and the focus ring on the active nav tab gets clipped — VoiceOver also stops announcing the active state after rotation. Happens on iOS Safari and Android Chrome.
Ethan Park: Repro on Pixel emulator. Looks like we recreate the header DOM on resize and we lose tabindex state. Also the focus outline sits inside a container with overflow:hidden.
Priya Singh: Two problems: 1) focus restoration after DOM replace, 2) visual clipping because of overflow/z-index. Need to avoid full DOM replacement for the header on orientation change.
Talia Mendes: I also noticed the active tab uses a 1px bottom border to indicate state. In high-contrast mode that border is invisible. Keyboard users rely on a visible focus ring.
Sasha Lee: For tabs we should use both an aria-selected on the tab and a visible focus/focus-visible style that meets 3:1 contrast for non-text controls. Proposed token: --tab-focus: 3px solid #ffe082 on dark backgrounds or 3px solid #005fcc on light backgrounds. Also prefer outline-offset so it doesn't clip.
Ethan Park: Example CSS to avoid clipping and preserve layout:
```css
.header { overflow: visible; z-index: 1000; } /* don't hide focus */
.tab:focus{outline:3px solid var(--tab-focus);outline-offset:2px;border-radius:4px;}
```
But we still need to handle the DOM recreation on rotation — better to keep active tab state in JS and reapply focus after reflow.
Priya Singh: On the screen reader side: ensure the active tab has aria-selected="true" and role="tab"/role="tablist" semantics. Also include aria-live="polite" region that announces navigation changes like "Switched to Models tab" for SR users when orientation triggers a reflow.
Talia Mendes: Will adding an aria-live cause double announcements when users click tabs normally? We should only update the live region when the change is triggered by orientation/restore, not on every click.
Sasha Lee: Add a small helper: updateLiveOnce(message) that sets the live region text and clears it after 1s. Only call that when restoreIsFromRotation is true.
Priya Singh: Also confirm heading structure after rotation — sometimes the H1 gets demoted to H2 due to template re-render. That breaks SR landmarks. Add a test that asserts heading hierarchy remains consistent.
Ethan Park: I'll add two fixes: 1) avoid replacing header node on resize, keep it persistent; 2) on any re-render, if active element was inside old header, schedule focus restore using requestAnimationFrame and element.focus({preventScroll: true}); 3) make sure parent containers don't have overflow:hidden during focus visuals.
Talia Mendes: Can we also capture a screenshot of the focus ring in dark, light, and high-contrast themes for the PR? Sasha requested that in past PRs.
Sasha Lee: Yes please. Also include a small Playwright scenario: set viewport to mobile, rotate viewport (swap width/height), tab to tabs, assert document.activeElement has role="tab" and aria-selected="true" after rotation. Add manual steps for VoiceOver iOS: open app, select tab, rotate device, confirm rotor reads the active tab as selected.
a11y-bot: Auto-scan: header re-render on resize flagged (risk: focus loss) \u26a0\ufe0f; focus-outline contrast check failed for current tokens \u274c; role=tab semantics missing on .nav-tabs \u274c. Report: https://redwood-internal/a11y/2067809999
Priya Singh: Thanks. Plan: 1) persistence for header node, 2) stronger focus token and outline-offset, 3) aria tab semantics + aria-live restore message only on rotation, 4) Playwright + manual VoiceOver checklist. I'll open a PR today and tag design+eng-runtime for z-index/overflow review.
Ethan Park: I'll prototype the focus persistence patch and tests. Tagging @eng-runtime for any global layout constraints that enforce overflow hidden on app-shell.
Talia Mendes: Great — thanks team. If we avoid replacing nodes during rotation, should be low-risk. Will add screenshots and voiceover steps to PR. :white_check_mark:
